summary: Evaluates existing GMPLS routing and signaling protocols against the Optical Channel Data Unit containers introduced in ITU-T G.709-2012. It is informational and looks at what changes might be needed.

eli5.summary: It checks whether old tools can handle the new boxes used in light-based cables.

subtitle: A gap analysis of what GMPLS routing and signaling cannot yet express about the 2012 OTN standard.

tldr.problem: ITU-T G.709-2012 added new fixed and flexible ODU containers to Optical Transport Networks, but existing GMPLS routing and signaling protocols were built around the 2001 revision and cannot describe or set up all of them.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC goes through each kind of OTN information (tributary slot granularity, tributary port number, signal types, unreserved bandwidth, terminating versus switching capability, multi-stage multiplexing, labels) and says what GMPLS already offers and what is missing.
tldr.outcome: It lists the gaps that new routing and signaling extensions must fill. It defines no protocol elements itself, so it carries no new security risk.

facts.label: Tolerance
facts.value: +/-100 ppm or +/-20 ppm by signal type

today: RFC 7096 is an Informational IETF-consensus document that has not been obsoleted or updated. It was written to identify the gaps that the separate OSPF and RSVP-TE extension documents for OTN address, with a framework in RFC 7062.

sections.title: Why an Evaluation Was Needed
sections.content:
GMPLS routing (RFC 4203, RFC 5307) and signaling (RFC 3473, RFC 4328) already control Optical Transport Networks (OTNs) based on the 2001 revision of G.709. The 2012 revision adds OTN features that GMPLS does not support, including new fixed and flexible Optical channel Data Unit (ODU) containers.

This document evaluates the existing GMPLS protocols against those requirements. Background and a framework are in RFC 7062, and separate OSPF and RSVP-TE extension documents address the gaps found here.

The OTN has a digital path layer (ODU) and a section layer (OTU). Some ODU types (ODU1 to ODU4) can act as client or server depending on the networking domain. Client ODU connections can ride over wavelength subnetworks (Case A), ODU links (Case B) or a mix (Case C).
sections.eli5: The cable boxes got upgraded, but the old trip-planning tools do not know about the new boxes. This paper checks what is missing.

sections.title: Tributary Slots, Granularity and Multiplexing
sections.content:
G.709 defines two tributary slot (TS) granularities, 1.25 Gbit/s and 2.5 Gbit/s, chosen per layer. If both ends of a link are new cards supporting both, the link uses 1.25 Gbit/s. If one end is an old card supporting only 2.5 Gbit/s, the link uses 2.5 Gbit/s.

In the data plane, the payload type (PT) value 0x20 supports ODTUjk only, and 0x21 supports ODTUk.ts, or ODTUk.ts and ODTUjk. The PT therefore ties to TS granularity. A fallback from PT=0x21 to PT=0x20 can make a link self-consistent, in which case the only reason to signal granularity is to give the correct label, since the label for PT=0x21 has twice the TS number of PT=0x20. Without that automatic fallback, RSVP-TE actions for a TS mismatch need to be defined.

In the control plane, the server granularity is transparent to an end-to-end ODUj, while the client granularity must be right for adaptation at the end nodes. The RFC concludes that routing must represent a link's TS granularity, PT capabilities and multiplexing hierarchy, and signaling must carry the TS granularity, PT and hierarchy encoding.
sections.eli5: Think of shipping crates with two kinds of shelves, thin and thick. If one side of a connection only has thin shelves, both sides must use thin ones, and the planner has to know which is which.

sections.title: Missing Signal and Bandwidth Information
sections.content:
The RFC walks through several kinds of information GMPLS cannot yet carry well.

  • Tributary Port Number: RFC 4328 supports only the deprecated auto-MSI mode. The association between TPN and TS has to be configured by the control plane and checked by the data plane, so RSVP-TE needs to support TPN assignment.
  • Signal type: OSPF and IS-IS can only advertise single-TS-type interfaces, with fixed bandwidth and implicit hierarchy, or variable bandwidth with no hierarchy. They cannot describe a mixed case such as ODUflex CBR and ODUflex packet. One Interface Switching Capability Descriptor (ISCD) per signal type would work but multiplies the number of ISCDs.
  • Bit rate and tolerance: ODUflex can have variable bit rates, so traffic parameters need an upgrade. Tolerance needs no upgrade, because a fixed value is defined per signal type.
  • Unreserved resources: they must be advertised per priority and per signal type. In the RFC's example, a TE link of three ODU3 component links with 32, 24 and 24 TSs available advertises 80 TSs and a MAX LSP bandwidth of 32 TSs, so a restoration attempt for two ODU3s fails and causes crankback.

Maximum LSP bandwidth and the eight priorities of RFC 4202 are also advertised inefficiently, but fixing that is not required to support OTNs.
sections.eli5: The planning tools know how much room is left in total, but not how that room is split up. So they may promise a big package a shelf cannot hold.

sections.title: Switching, Terminating and Multi-Stage Multiplexing
sections.content:
An interface may only switch a signal (forward it to the switching matrix without multiplexing or demultiplexing), only terminate it, or do both. Routing therefore has to separate terminating capability from switching capability. In the RFC's examples, a node that can extract an ODU0 only from an ODU2 interface must not be routed through an OTU3 link, and ODU2 bandwidth that can only be terminated cannot be used to restore an ODU2 LSP passing through, though it is still useful for an LSP ending at that node. The RFC notes this is a general, technology-independent GMPLS limitation.

Multi-stage multiplexing (for example ODU1 into ODU2 into ODU3) needs cascaded adaptation capabilities advertised together with matrix access constraints. The IETF structure for this is the Interface Adaptation Capability Descriptor (IACD) of RFC 6001. Counting free ODU1s is not enough, because spatial allocation matters: with ODU1s split 3+2 across two bundled component links, no ODU2 forwarding adjacency can be set up, while a 4+1 split allows one. Both the ISCD and the IACD need to be augmented.
sections.eli5: It matters not just how many small boxes are free, but where they sit. Five free boxes spread across two trucks may not fit into one big container.

sections.title: Generalized Label
sections.content: The ODUk label format of RFC 4328 could be updated for the new signal types, but it would be hard to extend for further ones. It may also not scale. Mapping an ODU3 into an ODU4 with 1.25 Gbit/s tributary slots would need 31 labels (31*4*8=992 bits), and an ODUflex into an ODU4 might need up to 80 labels (80*4*8=2560 bits). The RFC concludes that a new, flexible and scalable ODUk label format needs to be defined.
sections.eli5: The old way of naming each seat on the train takes a lot of writing for a big group. A shorter way to name many seats is needed.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The document evaluates OTN requirements against the existing routing and signaling mechanisms. It describes new types of information to carry, but it defines no new protocol elements. From a security standpoint it therefore adds no risk beyond what GMPLS protocols can already convey. For general MPLS and GMPLS security, the RFC points to the MPLS/GMPLS security framework in RFC 5920.
sections.eli5: This paper only lists what is missing and builds nothing new, so it makes nothing less safe.
